label: Levobupivacaine — systemic disposition + site absorption

parameters.label: apparent volume of distribution (reference adult)
parameters.covariate_model: reference-adult disposition (no covariate model; ~ bupivacaine, the S-enantiomer shares its disposition)

extraction.tier_rationale: Reference-adult LA disposition value (Tier-C by design). Levobupivacaine is the S-enantiomer of bupivacaine and shares its disposition closely; the load-bearing LA2 claim is the INTERMEDIATE cardiotoxicity, not the precise volume.
extraction.source_locator: Bardsley 1998; standard LA PK reference values (~ bupivacaine)
Bardsley 1998; standard LA PK reference values (~ bupivacaine)

extraction.tier_rationale: Site-absorption rank order robust; absolute ka Tier-C, applied site-wise (the site dominates the rate of rise; a drug-independent simplification shared across the LA models).

toxicity_thresholds.method_caveat: Volunteer i.v. study (Bardsley 1998). Levobupivacaine shares bupivacaine's local-anesthetic potency, so its CNS-symptom range is close to bupivacaine's; speed of rise and acidosis lower the threshold.
toxicity_thresholds.saturation_caveat: Saturable binding: this total-basis range under-predicts free-drug risk at high total concentration (the free fraction rises non-linearly; nonlinear model is v0.6 LA3).

toxicity_thresholds.method_caveat: Levobupivacaine's cardiovascular margin over its CNS-warning range is WIDER than racemic bupivacaine's (less negative inotropy and less avid cardiac Na-channel binding at equal dose; Bardsley 1998) but NARROWER than ropivacaine's — the intermediate ranking. Magnitude Tier-C; the load-bearing fact is the margin order bupivacaine < levobupivacaine < ropivacaine.
toxicity_thresholds.saturation_caveat: Saturable binding: this total-basis cardiovascular range under-predicts free-drug risk at high total concentration (v0.6 LA3).

extraction.tier_rationale: CVS thresholds are wide, method-dependent and ethically un-doseable in volunteers; Tier-C. The clinically load-bearing claim is the intermediate margin, not a precise number.

v0.6 LA2: the S-enantiomer that anchors the INTERMEDIATE point of the cardiotoxicity comparison (racemic bupivacaine > levobupivacaine > ropivacaine). Disposition ~ bupivacaine (Tier-C reference-adult); the curated, load-bearing claim is the intermediate cardiotoxicity_class + the wider-than-bupivacaine cardiovascular margin (Bardsley 1998).

source_review.reviewed_by: automated source cross-check (Claude Opus 4.8 via Hypnos research agents)
source_review.method: fetched FDA/EMA labels (DailyMed/SmPC), primary-paper PubMed abstracts, open implementations, and CrossRef, then compared each curated value against the fetched values
sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1873676/ (Bardsley 1998 - states Vss/CL could NOT be computed, drug measurable only 120 min)
source_review.notes: CITATION DISCREPANCY (values not changed): the record cites Bardsley 1998, but that paper EXPLICITLY could not compute Vss or clearance (a cardiovascular-effects study; levobupivacaine measurable only 120 min). The curated Vss 67 L / CL 0.5 L/min match the Chirocaine SmPC / 40 mg-IV volunteer data (Vss 66.9 L, CL 39 L/h = 0.65 L/min) reproduced in PMC3819850. HUMAN ACTION: re-cite to the Chirocaine SmPC / a levobupivacaine PK monograph, not Bardsley 1998.

notes: Systemic concentration only (NOT block efficacy, NOT a toxicity margin). Same Bateman absorption + one-compartment disposition as the other LA models; the LA2 point is the cardiotoxicity_class differentiation and the agent-choice CNS-to-CVS margin comparison surfaced via `hypnos la --agents`.
